newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: REPORT ON GUATEMALA STADIUM DISASTER DUE SOON.
newsitem.headline: REPORT ON GUATEMALA STADIUM DISASTER DUE SOON.

text.p: A presidential commission studying last week's soccer stadium tragedy in which 82 people were suffocated and crushed to death will make a report later this week, government officials said on Monday.
"We want to hear all the parties and we believe that we'll be able to turn in our report on Thursday," Oscar Berger, Guatemala City mayor and a member of the commission, told reporters.
President Alvaro Arzu charged the commission with finding out what caused the disaster and who was responsible.

Berger said the commission spent Monday meeting with soccer authorities who planned and managed the World Cup qualifying game between Guatemala and Costa Rica on Wednesday night in the Mateo Flores stadium.
Half an hour before kick-off, an unknown event in the overcrowded, standing-room-only terraces at one end of the stadium triggered a human avalanche.
Hundreds of people tumbled on top of each other, resulting in the worst stadium disaster in World Cup history.

The government has said a fight in the stands set off the tragic crush, but the local media have pointed fingers at the stadium's inadequate security and rampant ticket forgery that led to overcrowding in the 47,000-capacity stadium.

Eyewitnesses told reporters a pressure of people outside the stadium broke through a door at the top of the stands and set off the avalanche. Others said many of the victims died suffocated against a fence at the bottom of the stands.
The National Police Chief told reporters on Monday that investigators have ruled out the door theory and have determined that few people died pressed against the fence.
The police chief, Angel Conte Conjulun, said investigators found most of the blood was in the middle of the stands.
